name: System Prompts
description: Provides register-specific system prompt injection templates for normalizing user input across different communication registers (casual, academic, narrative, technical, direct). Implements Level 1 prompt engineering to interpret varied linguistic registers as precise technical queries.

types.name: str
types.description: String type for prompts and register identifiers

functions.name: get_system_prompt
functions.description: Retrieves the appropriate Level 1 system prompt injection based on detected register. Returns empty string for 'direct' register. Falls back to GENERIC_NORMALIZATION for unknown registers. Accepts either Register enum instances (with .value attribute) or string values.

inputs.name: detected_register
inputs.description: The detected input register. Can be Register enum with .value attribute or string. Expected values: 'casual', 'academic', 'narrative', 'technical', 'direct'

inputs.name: target_register
inputs.description: Optional target register override (currently unused in implementation)

postconditions: Returns register-specific prompt from _REGISTER_PROMPTS if key exists
Returns GENERIC_NORMALIZATION for unknown register values

functions.name: inject_system_prompt
functions.description: Prepends a register normalization instruction to an existing system prompt. Idempotent operation: if injection is already present in existing_system, returns unchanged. Handles empty/falsy inputs gracefully.

inputs.name: existing_system
inputs.description: The existing system prompt to augment

postconditions: Returns existing_system unchanged if injection is empty/falsy
Returns injection if existing_system is empty/falsy
Returns existing_system unchanged if injection substring already present
Idempotent: calling with same arguments produces same result

invariants: GENERIC_NORMALIZATION is a constant fallback prompt for unknown registers
get_system_prompt always returns a string (empty or populated)
inject_system_prompt is idempotent: multiple applications produce same result as single application

data_access.rationale: Pure functions operating on module-level constants. No I/O or persistent state.

authority.rationale: Owns the mapping between detected linguistic registers and corresponding system prompt injections
